newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices seen mixed - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices seen mixed - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen mixed amid regional differences in marketings, livestock dealers said.

Western Corn Belt hog dealers said prices were expected to be pressured by more than adequate hog supplies. Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $57.50 to $58.00 per cwt.

Eastern Belt hog supplies were not as adequate, which could underpin prices in Illinois and Indiana, several dealers said. Illinois top prices for hogs at the plant were seen at $57.50, the dealers said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs delivered to plants could range from $58.50 to $59.00, they said.
"There wasn't a very big run today and it doesn't look any better on Tuesday," one Indiana dealer said. "However, we've had decent demand for what hogs we do get."

Pork prices at midday were mixed but trended mostly lower. Fresh loins were not tested at midday, butts were up $1.00 to $2.00 per cwt, bellies were down $1.00-$3.00 and lean trimmings were steady to $3.00 lower, USDA said in its central U.S. carlot pork report.
